EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows dominant aliphatic C–H stretches (2988, 2940, 2880 cm⁻¹) and a single strong C=O stretch at 1731 cm⁻¹, characteristic of a saturated ester rather than a ketone (≈1715 cm⁻¹) or an anhydride (which would give two C=O bands near 1760 & 1820 cm⁻¹). Ester C–O stretches are present at 1114, 1100 and 1152 cm⁻¹, and C–C–O / CH₃ rocking modes of an isopropyl group typically give bands near 830–880 cm⁻¹ (observed 831 & 868 cm⁻¹) and ~780 cm⁻¹. Candidate 6 (CCC(=O)OC(C)C, isopropyl propionate) contains only saturated alkyl groups and a single ester carbonyl, fitting all these key features, while other ester-containing candidates have additional functional groups (OH, NO₂, NCO, second C=O) whose characteristic Raman bands are absent.
